card.name: Exceptions after 'all but one' or 'only'
card.fires_on: Words that complete an exception or negative in a near-universal statement, such as the number after 'all but', or 'not' and 'n't' after 'the only ones who' or 'the one who'. It also fires on 'differences' after 'no clinically meaningful'.

modes.label: Number after all but
modes.description: The count of exceptions right after 'all but' in a statement about nearly everyone or everything.
modes.example: LVEF recovered to ≥ 50% in all but<< one>> patient.

modes.label: Negation in the only-ones clause
modes.description: A negation or dissent word that ends a clause about the lone exceptions to a general statement.
modes.example: The one student who did<< not>> meet the standard missed it by only one

modes.label: No meaningful differences
modes.description: The word after 'no' or 'anything' that states an absence or an exception.
modes.example: there are no clinically meaningful<< differences>> between the biosimilar product and the reference

card.writes: It seems to push toward words that say something is rare or small, such as '少见' and '很小'.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a sentence names the few exceptions to a rule, as in 'all but one' or 'the only ones who don't'.
